standard_pattern.note: Standard word order places most adjectives AFTER the noun in Spanish

shortened_adjectives.rule: ADJETIVOS CORTOS (Apocope) — Certain adjectives drop their final '-o' when placed BEFORE a masculine singular noun

affected_adjectives.example: El buen chico. / ¡Qué tenga un buen día!
affected_adjectives.english: The good boy. / Have a good day!

affected_adjectives.example: Hoy es mi primer día de clases de español.
affected_adjectives.english: Today is my first day of Spanish classes.

shortened_adjectives.note: These shortened forms only apply before MASCULINE SINGULAR nouns. Feminine forms (buena, mala, primera, tercera, alguna, ninguna) are NOT shortened.

example_sentences.spanish: El gallo no ha cantado todavía.

example_sentences.english: There were a lot of people.
example_sentences.grammar_note: Imperfect of haber (había) for existence in the past

example_sentences.spanish: Es un buen día para el partido.
example_sentences.english: It's a good day for the match.

common_descriptive_adjectives.note: enfadado is more common in Spain
